nodes.name: Lithium iron phosphate cathode material suppliers
nodes.mechanism: Battery cell manufacturers purchase more LFP cathode powder as utility-scale developers specify lower-cost, longer-life chemistries.
nodes.logic: Utility projects are large, repetitive procurements that concentrate purchasing power among cathode suppliers. LFP is widely used for grid batteries, so a faster buildout translates into higher volume and price premiums during periods of tight precursor supply.

nodes.name: Power conversion system suppliers
nodes.mechanism: Every grid-scale battery installation requires inverters, transformers, and controls, so equipment suppliers receive higher order intake.
nodes.logic: Power conversion systems account for a meaningful share of project capital cost and must be sized with each battery block. Because the number of in-service systems rises with project completions, revenue growth can exceed the underlying battery gigawatt growth as earlier vintages are replaced or repowered.

nodes.name: Contracted utility-scale storage developers
nodes.mechanism: Independent power producers and developers sell energy, capacity, and ancillary services from new battery projects under long-term contracts.
nodes.logic: Accelerated interconnection queues and grid-operator procurement targets expand the addressable project pipeline. Developers with contracted portfolios convert signed offtake agreements into construction revenue and recurring cash flows faster than merchant-only peers.

nodes.name: Natural gas peaker plant operators
nodes.mechanism: Batteries displace gas turbines from peak-shifting and ancillary-service roles, reducing run hours and capacity payments.
nodes.logic: Grid batteries can respond faster than peakers and have low marginal cost, so they win the peak-priced operating hours first. Peaker operators lose the most lucrative dispatch periods while still carrying fixed costs, compressing plant-level margins before outright retirement.

nodes.name: Pumped hydro storage operators
nodes.mechanism: Lithium-ion batteries capture frequency regulation and daily arbitrage revenue that historically accrued to pumped-storage assets.
nodes.logic: Pumped hydro plants have long construction times and limited siting options, while battery projects can enter service in under three years. As battery capacity saturates the premium grid services, pumped hydro assets face lower clearing prices and longer payback periods on new investments.

nodes.name: Lithium carbonate and hydroxide refiners
nodes.mechanism: Higher LFP cathode output pulls more lithium chemicals through the supply chain.
nodes.logic: Cathode plants are primary industrial buyers of battery-grade lithium chemicals. When utility buildout accelerates, their offtake volumes rise and contract pricing tightens, so refiners absorb volume growth before it reaches mining companies.

nodes.name: Power semiconductor and module suppliers
nodes.mechanism: Inverter manufacturers buy more insulated-gate bipolar transistor and silicon carbide modules to meet rising power-conversion demand.
nodes.logic: Power modules are a constrained, high-value component inside every storage inverter. As inverter production scales to match the buildout, module suppliers gain volume leverage and can pass through shortages more effectively than downstream assemblers.

nodes.name: Battery and substation electrical contractors
nodes.mechanism: Developers hire specialized contractors to install battery racks, thermal management, and grid interconnection equipment.
nodes.logic: Each utility-scale project requires a discrete construction crew and substation upgrade, so contractor revenue is directly tied to project starts. The specialized labor pool is relatively small, allowing qualified firms to expand margins as demand outpaces the available workforce.

nodes.name: Gas turbine original equipment manufacturers
nodes.mechanism: Fewer new peaker plants are ordered as utilities choose batteries for incremental capacity.
nodes.logic: Turbine OEMs rely on new unit sales and long-term service contracts for revenue growth. A sustained shift from gas peakers to batteries removes a predictable source of large new orders and shrinks the installed base that generates aftermarket revenue.

nodes.name: Pumped hydro turbine and equipment suppliers
nodes.mechanism: Developers delay or cancel pumped-storage projects as batteries capture the same grid services.
nodes.logic: Pumped hydro equipment orders depend on a small number of large greenfield projects. When lithium-ion storage shortens development cycles and wins procurement contracts, the pipeline for new pumped hydro contracts narrows, leaving equipment suppliers dependent on maintenance rather than expansion.

nodes.name: Lithium-ion battery recycling service providers
nodes.mechanism: A larger installed base creates more end-of-life batteries and manufacturing scrap to process.
nodes.logic: Recyclers need feedstock scale to cover fixed plant costs. Faster utility deployment increases both future retired packs and current production scrap, tightening long-term cathode material supply and improving the economics of recycling as a source of battery-grade inputs.

nodes.name: Spodumene and hard-rock lithium miners
nodes.mechanism: Refiners raise concentrate purchases to expand lithium chemical output.
nodes.logic: Hard-rock miners supply the feedstock for the principal refining routes used by LFP supply chains. Demand from refiners grows faster than mine supply can respond, lifting long-term contract prices and improving project returns for producers with permitted reserves.

nodes.name: Silicon carbide wafer suppliers
nodes.mechanism: Power module makers increase silicon carbide wafer purchases for higher-efficiency inverters.
nodes.logic: Silicon carbide wafers are a key input for next-generation power modules used in large inverters. As inverter manufacturers upgrade product lines to handle higher voltages and efficiencies, wafer demand grows ahead of module shipments, tightening supply and strengthening pricing.

nodes.name: Gas turbine forging and casting suppliers
nodes.mechanism: Turbine OEMs order fewer forged rotors, casings, and superalloy components as production slows.
nodes.logic: Forgings are long-lead items tied to new unit manufacturing schedules. A sustained decline in gas turbine orders reduces the volume of forgings and castings placed on the foundry floor, pressuring capacity utilization and margins at specialized suppliers.
